Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the EcoNova Renewables Inc. Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the session, please press star then 1 on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss EcoNova Renewables's results for the Q4 2023. Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Financial Officer; Sophia Chen, Chief Development Officer; Liam Ortiz, Chief Technology Officer; Nadia Patel, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of federal securities laws. These statements are based on our current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Jordan, and good morning, everyone. EcoNova Renewables delivered exceptional results in the Q4 2023, showcasing our leadership in the renewable energy sector. Our success is attributable to our innovative technologies, strategic partnerships, and unwavering commitment to sustainability.

Today, I want to highlight seven key aspects of our performance: our overall performance highlights and key achievements; capital expenditure and operating expense details; debt levels and financing costs; construction progress and commercial operation dates; PPA pricing trends and contract extensions; capital recycling and asset sale transactions; and our strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter and year.

These achievements position us strongly for continued growth. Now, I'll hand over the call to Marcus Hale to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. Our financial performance in the Q4 2023 was outstanding. Revenue reached $1.28 billion, representing a 32% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production from our integrated clean energy value chain, spanning upstream solar module manufacturing, wind turbine supply, downstream EPC, BESS, and LDES solutions. Our gross margin expanded to 42%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $480 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing, yet disciplined at just 7% YoY growth despite 35% portfolio expansion. Net income was $162 million, or $0.78 per diluted share. We ended the quarter with $1.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are raising our full-year guidance for revenue to $5.2-5.5 billion and earnings accordingly.

To give more context on these results, let me expand on our overall performance highlights and key achievements. We're thrilled with how we've solidified our position as a leader in the integrated clean energy space. In Q4, revenue hit $1.28 billion, up 32% year-over-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter, surpassing our guidance and consensus by 12%. This was powered by a 45% surge in U.S. EPC and project development, boosted by IRA tax credits like 45X advanced manufacturing production credits and 48E clean electricity investment credits. Solar module sales from our high-efficiency N-type TOPCon bifacial panels at 23.5% efficiency brought in $420 million, up 28% YoY, as we ramped our 5 GW Texas fab to 85% utilization.

Profitability shone through with adjusted EBITDA at $285 million, up 42% YoY and margins at 22.3%—our best in three years—thanks to optimized supply chains where silicon wafer prices dropped 15% quarter-over-quarter from Chinese oversupply and 70% vertical integration of our bill of materials. Free cash flow reached $210 million, up from $145 million last year, funding $120 million in share repurchases and a 25% dividend increase to $0.22 per share. Our backlog hit a record $18.5 billion, or 4.2 times revenue visibility through 2027, with 60% at fixed-price PPAs averaging $42 per MWh, below the U.S. wholesale average of $58 per MWh.

Operationally, we commissioned 1.2 GW of new capacity, growing our portfolio to 12.8 GW across solar PV, onshore wind, and hybrid BESS—up 25% YoY. Standouts include the 450 MWac Desert Sun Solar plus 200 MWh BESS hybrid in Arizona at 32% capacity factor using AI curtailment optimization for ERCOT and CAISO integration, avoiding 650,000 metric tons of CO2 yearly. Our 300 MW WindForge onshore turbines at 60% capacity factor powered the 250 MW Prairie Winds farm in Oklahoma under a 15-year corporate PPA with a Fortune 100 tech firm at $35 per MWh. Tech-wise, Gen3 TOPCon cells hit 25.2% efficiency in pilots, and 150 MWh vanadium flow LDES in a California pilot showed 20-year degradation-free performance at 85% round-trip efficiency.

Regionally, North America drove 55% of revenue at $704 million, up 40% with $180 million from IRA PTC/ITC. Europe added 25% or $320 million via EU Green Deal wins like 500 MW Spanish solar EPC and North Sea O&M. APAC grew 35% to $192 million on India and Australia deals, plus Brazil's first 50 MW floating solar.

Strategically, our $450 million CleanFlow Batteries acquisition added LFP tech and 2 GWh capacity, growing BESS backlog 60% with DOE loans. JVs with Siemens Gamesa and Panasonic mitigated tariffs. U.S. utility-scale solar EPC share rose to 8.2%, LCOE at $28 per MWh versus industry $34 per MWh. We cut Scope 1&2 emissions 95% from 2019, topping S&P ESG and MSCI Leaders. This sets up $6-7 billion FY2024 revenue at 24% EBITDA margins.

Shifting to capital expenditure, or CAPEX, and operating expense, or OPEX details—these form the backbone of our growth as we scale our 12 GW global portfolio of utility-scale solar PV, onshore and offshore wind, and BESS. Our approach delivered 22% YoY adjusted EBITDA growth to $850 million for FY2023, keeping net debt-to-EBITDA at 3.2x.

CAPEX totaled $1.25 billion for FY2023, up 28% from $975 million in 2022, amid IRA and REPowerEU tailwinds unlocking $2.8 billion in low-cost financing. Q4 CAPEX was $420 million, ahead due to EPC procurement. Breakdown: Solar PV 52% or $650 million for 1.2 GW U.S. pipeline including 550 MW Rattlesnake Solar at 90% mechanical completion; module costs up 12% YoY to $0.28/W DC from polysilicon constraints, mitigated by PPAs with LONGi and JinkoSolar at 15% spot discount, LCOE $25-28/MWh with IRA ITC. Wind 28% or $350 million for India Gujarat hybrid and UK Dogger Bank extension; turbine CAPEX $1.4M/MW up 18%, but hybrids at 45% capacity factors. BESS/Grid 15% or $190 million for 800 MWh U.S. deployments at $220/kWh down 8% YoY via CATL/LG and IRA bonuses. Manufacturing/R&D 5% or $60 million for Arizona perovskite fab targeting 25% efficiency.

U.S. CAPEX up 45% to $850 million on IRA; Europe down 5% to $250 million on permits; APAC steady at $150 million. FY2024 guide $1.6-1.8 billion, 60% U.S./Australia, hedging 70% commodities for 10-15% deflation.

OPEX was $480 million FY2023, up 7% YoY or $40/kW annualized down from $48/kW, 24% of revenue versus 29%. O&M 42% or $202 million with 28% solar CUF, 38% wind, $25 million AI savings via GE Vernova digital twins cutting downtime 22%. SG&A 28% or $134 million at 11% revenue. R&D/Tech 22% or $106 million on green H2 electrolyzers and iron-air batteries. Other 8% or $38 million. U.S. $35/kW, Europe $50/kW, India $28/kW. Scale dilutes fixed costs 12% per GW, prioritizing >12% IRR assets.

Now, on debt levels and financing costs, as we scale our 12 GW pipeline—wait, 15 GW in some, but consistent 12 GW operating plus pipeline. Total gross debt $5.2 billion end-Q4, up 8% YoY from $650 million non-recourse for Rattlesnake and Viking Wind. Net debt $4.1 billion with $1.1 billion cash from 8.2 GW portfolio at 95%+ factors on PPAs. Net debt/EBITDA 3.4x, below 4.5x covenant and peers.

72% long-term fixed-rate non-recourse, 18-year tenor matching PPAs; $2.1 billion green bonds at SOFR +145 bps. Revolver 15% drawn of $1.5 billion. Effective rate 4.2% down 30 bps via $400 million prepays using tax equity. Floating 28% hedged to 2027. U.S. IRA transferability cut costs 150 bps; Europe up to 5.1%; APAC BBSW +220 bps.

Forward, $2 billion sustainability RCF saves 10-15 bps; $1 billion green bond shelf; debt to $6-6.5B YE2025, delever to 3.2x.

On construction progress and commercial operation dates, we have 12.4 GW under construction, 45% of backlog, mobilizing 1.2 GW/quarter with First Solar and Vestas partners. YTD 2.5 million m3 concrete, 1.8 million modules; domestic content 45% for IRA adders, lead times 12 weeks.

U.S. Desert Horizon 750 MWdc solar +1.2 GWh BESS 92% complete, mechanical 85%, COD Q4 2024 with Meta PPA. Texas Lone Star 450 MW wind +900 MWh LDES 76% complete, COD Q1 2025. Offshore Pacific Winds 400 MW 42% complete, COD H2 2026. Australia Waratah 600 MW 68%, COD Q3 2025. Brazil Ventos 350 MW 81%, COD Q2 2025. Floating solar Portugal 20%, COD H1 2026; iron-flow BESS pilot energizing now.

4.2 GW CODs FY2024 adding $1.1B revenue; 7.8 GW 2025.

Regarding PPA pricing trends and contract extensions, U.S. solar PPAs softened to $24/MWh, wind $28/MWh per NREL, but hybrids $35-40/MWh in ERCOT. CAISO $18-22/MWh; Europe €35-45/MWh up 10-15%; Australia A$60-70/MWh. We closed 450 MW new at $29/MWh blended, 250 MW solar $32/MWh with hyperscaler, 300 MW wind $31/MWh.

60% hybrids capture peaks; extensions on 1.2 GW added $450M NPV at 12% uplift, e.g., Midwest wind to 2040 at $29/MWh. Southeast solar resets 15-20%. 85% backlog PPA'd, 15-20% merchant at $55/MWh peaks. Prices trough 2025 then rebound on IRA, data centers.

Finally, capital recycling and asset sales: Q3 sales 750 MW for $1.2B, up 25% QoQ. 400 MW U.S. solar to Brookfield at 1.9x, 8.2% yield, 14.2% IRR; 350 MW Texas wind to Clearway at 12% IRR. YTD $3.1B recycled: 60% new projects, 25% debt paydown to 3.2x, 15% emerging tech.

Multiples up 20-25% post-IRA; Europe 1.7x; APAC 15% IRR. U.S. 65% sales with IRA stack; Europe hybrids; India agrivoltaics. Guide $4.5-5.5B 2025 at 14% IRRs. Self-funds 70% pipeline.

I'll now turn the call over to Sophia Chen to discuss our project development activities.

Sophia Chen:
Thank you, Marcus. Our project development pipeline continues to expand, with 28 GW of projects under development across solar PV, onshore/offshore wind, and BESS. We're advancing land rights, permits, and PPAs, expecting several new projects online soon to boost revenue. We're pursuing acquisitions and partnerships for acceleration.

Liam, can you update on technological advancements?

Liam Ortiz:
Thank you, Sophia. We're dedicated to innovation in renewables. R&D targets efficiency, reliability, affordability. Breakthroughs in N-type TOPCon bifacial at 23.8% efficiency ramping to 20 GW; perovskite tandems to 30%+ by 2025 slashing LCOE under $20/MWh; LFP BESS for 4-hour projects; solid-state prototypes at 800 Wh/kg; 100 MW PEM electrolyzer for $2/kg H2. Hybrids yield 12%+ IRR.

Next, Nadia will discuss sustainability.

Nadia Patel:
Thank you, Liam. Sustainability is core at EcoNova. We're minimizing impact with goals for carbon reductions, efficiency gains, resource management. 95% Scope 1&2 cuts; community engagement; SBTi-validated sourcing; circularity to 95% by 2026 aligning EU regs.

Now, Raj will provide operational highlights.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Nadia. Operations strong, optimizing efficiency, reliability. Best practices in asset management, maintenance, supply chain; employee training. AI predictive maintenance cut downtime 22%; drone inspections; BESS degradation 1.2%/year; high CUF across assets.

I'll turn it back to Elena for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Raj. To summarize, EcoNova had an exceptional Q4 2023. To expand on our strategic priorities and outlook, as we close strong quarters, our focus is scaling high-margin clean tech amid electrification and decarbonization. $18.5B backlog gives two years visibility; IEA sees 5,500 GW renewables by 2030.

Pillars: Technology leadership—$160M FY25 R&D for perovskite 28.5% lab efficiency; BESS 2.5 GWh Q4 shipments; H2 pilot Q1 2025. Geographic expansion—U.S. $450M credits, 1.2 GW PPAs; Europe 25% backlog on REPowerEU, 800 MW turbines; APAC 5 GW Adani deal, India $60M Q4; LatAm hydro-solar. Supply chain—$300M CAPEX for U.S. line, 95% circularity. Capital allocation—$1.2B liquidity, $180M Q4 CAPEX, $100M repurchases, M&A.

Q4 guide $440-460M revenue 24-27% growth, EBITDA $110-115M 25-25.5% margins. FY25 raised to $1.95-2.05B revenue 30-35% growth, EBITDA $500-525M. Backlog 40% H1 conversion; $1.7T global investment.

We're shaping the energy transition for EPS $2.15-2.25 FY25, 15% ROIC.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the floor for questions. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Kim with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Sarah. International expansion is a key pillar. In Europe, now 25% of backlog, REPowerEU's €300 billion drives offshore wind and electrolyzers; we're shipping 800 MW turbines Q4 for Baltic farms at 55% capacity factors, adding €1.2 billion pipeline via UK CfD and German EEG. APAC leverages stabilizing $0.22/W prices; 5 GW supply with Adani for India's 500 GW target, Q4 India $60 million; Vietnam/Indonesia JETPs for 2 GW floating solar. Latin America grows 10% with Brazil/Chile hydro-solar at 18% IRRs. Tailored to policies, diversified 60/25/15 U.S./EU/APAC mitigates risks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Torres with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Torres:
How are you addressing the challenge of intermittency associated with renewable energy sources?

Liam Ortiz:
Great question, Mike. Intermittency is core to our innovation. Hybrids with co-located BESS—60% new PPAs—like 500 MW/2 GWh Texas with trackers for 12%+ IRR, reduce curtailment 30%. LDES like iron-air 100-hour discharge and vanadium flow at 85% efficiency firm baseload. Green H2 from 100 MW electrolyzer uses curtailment for $2/kg. AI optimization, trackers boost yields 5-7%; solid-state batteries for density. Positions us for ancillary revenue in CAISO/ERCOT.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Can you discuss the impact of government subsidies and tax incentives on your profitability?

Marcus Hale:
Absolutely, Lisa. Subsidies are transformative. IRA's $369B unlocked $450M FY25 PTC/ITC, 45X credits for fabs, transferability cut financing 150 bps, 30-50% ITC adders, 45Y PTC for domestic content. U.S. platform 45% CAPEX surge; $1.2B direct pay credits. REPowerEU €300B for Europe; India's PLI, Australia's CIS. Tax equity flips boost IRRs 16%; passthroughs drop OPEX intensity. Mitigate phaseouts via transferability; peers underexecute without. Margins to 26%, EPS CAGR 20%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Ruiz:
What are your expectations for electricity demand growth in the coming years?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, David. Demand surges from electrification, data centers—McKinsey 100 GW AI by 2030—hyperscalers' 40 GW PPAs. IEA 5,500 GW renewables; BloombergNEF $1.7T investment 2025, storage CAPEX doubles $65B. Corporate PPAs from Google/Amazon de-risk; duck curve, NEM 3.0 drive hybrids. Our backlog captures this for 30-35% revenue growth FY25, ROIC 15%.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Elena Vasquez for any closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of EcoNova Renewables. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
